I'm late to the party for this, but it's worth noting that if someone expects to be able to whip up a gasifier and turn the key on their Civic... well, their gonna have a bad time. Basically, anything with fuel injection is out, not withstanding a major stripping of the engine and ancillaries. Tier 3+ engines are probably out as well (anyone who builds engines for the US market has to adhere to the EPA horseshit). If I recall correctly, woodgas can be pretty variable, ranging from almost non-combustible to naptha. Because of this, high compression engines (above 7:1) suffer from knocking. If you're dragging a disker or generating electricity with a modern engine, this is a huge issue since aluminium blocks, con-rods, pistons, cam bearings, etc suffer from fatigue. Reducing the compression ratio is a good solution but will substantially reduce the performance of the engine. Note that during the war, the engines of the time were designed for fuel with octane around 40, and required massive displacements to get moderate power. The Wright Flyer made something like 12hp from 120 cu in.

Woodgas shines in burner applications such as light and heat. If you want to make engine fuel, gasifying plastics and distillating the fractions would get you further ahead. (and make you a god in the community: "oh here, let me refill your bic lighter for you")
